title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
date_evidence: Date: 24.7.2026 (publication date); 8 July 2026 (adoption date); OJ Reference: L series, 2026/1744
key_claim: Recital 2 states that the delayed preparation of standards and the delayed establishment of governance and conformity-assessment frameworks at national level resulted in a compliance burden heavier than expected; Recital 40 sets the new dates of 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I).
frame_summary: The regulation's own recitals frame the postponement as necessitated by the EU's own institutional and technical unreadiness (standards, conformity assessment, national competent authorities), not as a discretionary relief measure granted to industry.
verbatim_quote: The experience gathered from the implementation of the parts of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 that already apply can inform the implementation of those parts that are yet to apply. In this context, the delayed preparation of standards, which provide technical solutions for providers of high-risk AI systems to ensure compliance with their obligations under that Regulation, and the delayed establishment of the governance and the conformity assessment frameworks at national level has resulted in a compliance burden that is heavier than expected.
verbatim_list: Article 113 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the dates of entry into force and application of that Regulation, in particular that the general date of application is 2 August 2026.

Therefore, it is appropriate that the date of application of Sections 1, 2 and 3 of Chapter III is set to 2 December 2027 for AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III, and to 2 August 2028 for AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I.

title: AI Omnibus enters into force
date_evidence: The article was published on 27 July 2026, with a last update noted as 31 July 2026.
key_claim: The Commission frames the AI Omnibus as a targeted simplification preserving safeguards, with high-risk Annex III rules starting 2 December 2027 and Annex I rules starting 2 August 2028.
frame_summary: The Commission's own communications frame the delay as a calibrated simplification exercise that protects safety, the official/consensus framing this scan contrasts with the readiness evidence.
verbatim_quote: The AI Omnibus, proposed as part of the digital omnibus package on 19 November 2025, delivers a targeted simplification of the AI rulebook while preserving strong safeguards for people's safety and fundamental rights.

title: Standardisation of the AI Act
key_claim: As of the Commission's own tracker (updated 03/08/2026), only one of the ten requested harmonised standards, prEN 18286 on quality management, had reached public enquiry, as of 30 October 2025.
frame_summary: The regulator's own standards tracker corroborates, from the Commission's own record, that the technical infrastructure for a presumption of conformity is still nascent.
verbatim_quote: On 30 October 2025, prEN 18286: Artificial Intelligence - Quality Management System for EU AI Act Regulatory Purposes became the first harmonised standard for AI to enter public enquiry

title: Europe's regulatory double bind
key_claim: As of June 2026 no JTC 21 harmonised standard had been cited in the Official Journal, conformity assessment bodies remain largely undesignated, and certification timelines stretch nine to twenty-four months.
frame_summary: CEPR frames the postponement as a genuine sovereignty double bind (enforce and risk trade retaliation, or retreat and cede governance capacity), while also reporting that Big Tech pushback, not only technical readiness, shaped the Commission's decision.

title: What came into force with the EU's AI Act this week, and what didn't
key_claim: European Parliament negotiators backed the compromise on the grounds that the technical standards underpinning compliance for high-risk AI systems were not ready in time; transparency duties took effect 2 August 2026 with fines up to 15 million euros or 3% of global turnover.
frame_summary: Quality journalism corroborates, via named EU officials and negotiators, that unready technical standards, not only business relief, drove the postponement vote.

title: EU Digital Omnibus on AI Enters Into Force
key_claim: The Commission introduced the Omnibus in response to practical implementation difficulties: delays in designating national competent authorities and conformity assessment bodies, and the absence of harmonised standards, guidance and compliance tools.
frame_summary: Law-firm client advisory corroborates, from a compliance-planning perspective, that the delay's proximate cause is institutional and technical unreadiness rather than discretionary relief.
verbatim_quote: The European Commission introduced the proposal in response to practical implementation difficulties under the AI Act, including delays in the designation of national competent authorities and conformity assessment bodies, as well as the absence of harmonized standards, guidance and other compliance tools for high-risk AI systems.
verbatim_list: On July 27, 2026, the EU's Digital Omnibus on Artificial Intelligence (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council) (the "Digital Omnibus") entered into force, three days after its publication in the Official Journal

title: Digital Omnibus IA : le report qui n'en est pas un
key_claim: French legal commentary quotes the regulation's own recital: the delay in availability of harmonised standards, common specifications and alternative guidance, plus delays in setting up national competent authorities, jeopardised the effective entry into application of the obligations, justifying moving the date from 2 August 2026.
frame_summary: Argues, in French legal-practice terms and citing the regulation's own recital verbatim, that the change is a redistribution of compliance obligations across time rather than simple relief.
verbatim_quote: Selon ses propres motifs, le retard dans la disponibilité des normes harmonisées, des spécifications communes et des orientations alternatives, ainsi que le retard dans la mise en place des autorités nationales compétentes, faisaient peser un risque sérieux sur l'entrée en application effective de ces obligations et sur les coûts de mise en conformité, au point de ne plus justifier le maintien de la date initiale du 2 août 2026.
